diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the compacted transition function $\rho=1$ in $K_0$ and vanishes away from $K_0$ without any smoothness requirement

issues.failure_explanation: The proof multiplies the state equation by (1-rho)*varphi*phi^eps and needs the gradient of this product. The paper allows rho to be merely measurable, for example an indicator function, so the product is not in L^2(H^1_0) and nabla(rho) does not exist. Even if one reads the identity as a statement about local energy densities, passing to the limit against the bounded weight varphi(1-rho) is not justified. Convergence of the measures a^eps grad(phi^eps).grad(phi^eps) only holds against continuous test functions. Testing against a general L^infty weight needs equi-integrability, for instance from a Meyers-type estimate, and none is invoked. The limits for phi^eps and psi^eps therefore rest on an unsupported step. (The A grad(phi_0), grad(psi^eps) on the right-hand side is also a typo for phi^eps.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a contained argument for the weighted limits. Either use higher integrability (Meyers) of grad(phi^eps) and grad(psi^eps) to get equi-integrability of the energy densities and weak convergence against L^infty weights, or prove the bound for smooth rho and pass to the limit by approximation.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise bound |A-B| <= C rho(1-rho) for general measurable rho, and the corollary built on the same argument, are not established as written. The error analysis in Section 3 does not use them, and for rho=chi_K the conclusion B=A follows from locality of H-convergence.
issues.title: Proof of the H-limit bound tests with (1-rho)*phi, which is not admissible for a non-smooth rho
issues.why_classification: The repair is a self-contained lemma or approximation argument that leaves the statement and the proof architecture intact. The affected results are peripheral to the main error estimates.

issues.failure_explanation: Testing with V=delta U_k gives (b grad U_k, grad(U_k-U_{k-1})). The step to (1/2)(b grad U_k,grad U_k)-(1/2)(b grad U_{k-1},grad U_{k-1}) uses the scalar identity a(a-b)=(1/2)(a-b)^2+(1/2)(a^2-b^2). That identity needs (b grad U_k, grad U_{k-1}) = (b grad U_{k-1}, grad U_k), i.e. a symmetric b. The class M(lambda,Lambda;D) allows non-symmetric matrices, and the paper itself treats transposes in the dual problem and in Section 2. For non-symmetric b an antisymmetric cross term (1/2)((b^T-b)grad U_k, grad U_{k-1}) remains. It is not controlled, so (sta2) is unproved in the stated generality.

failure_location.quote: Since $b^\varepsilon_H$ is time-independent, summing up the above inequality from $1$ to $m$, we obtain~\eqref{sta2}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume that a^eps and A_H, hence A and b_H^eps, are symmetric. Alternatively supply a separate argument for the non-symmetric case, for example a Kato-type square-root or discrete analyticity estimate.
issues.overall_effect: Estimate (sta4) and hence the H^1 and time-derivative bounds (thm12) and (thm13) of Theorem 3.5 are not proved for non-symmetric coefficients. This is the estimate that removes the Delta t^{-1/2} factor. The L^2 bound (thm11) uses only (sta1) and is unaffected.
issues.title: Discrete H^1-type stability estimate uses symmetry of the coefficient, which is not assumed
issues.why_classification: Restricting to symmetric coefficients is a limited weakening that keeps a recognizably comparable result, and all numerical examples are symmetric. Treating the general case would need a genuinely new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The superapproximation property A3 holds only for elements with h_tau <= d, and the proof of Lemma 3.8 invokes it with the added phrase 'we have assumed h <= d'. This hypothesis appears in none of the statements of Lemma 3.8, Theorem 3.7 or Theorem 3.9, which are claimed with constants independent of d, h and H. The statements are therefore not valid as written for h > d. The mesh near the defect must be fine relative to the defect size, which is a genuine regime restriction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis h <= d (the maximal mesh size on K is at most the defect diameter) to Lemma 3.8, Theorem 3.7 and Theorem 3.9.
issues.overall_effect: The interior energy estimates are proved only under h <= d, but are stated for all mesh sizes and defect diameters.
issues.title: Interior estimate and its dependents need an unstated condition h <= d
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard mesh-resolution condition fixes the statements. The method, the estimates and their rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds ||grad(I-R_h)(omega u_k)||_{L^2(K)} by the infimum of ||grad(omega u_k - V)||_{L^2(K)} (the norm over K), plus other terms. In the last display this infimum silently becomes one over L^2(K_0), and the same L^2(K_0) appears in (3.6). An infimum of a K_0-norm cannot bound the K-norm, because a V that is good on K_0 may be arbitrarily bad on K minus K_0. The theorem as stated is therefore stronger than what is proved. Theorem 3.9 and the introduction use the L^2(K) version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L^2(K_0) by L^2(K) in the infimum term of (3.6) and in the last line of the proof, matching the proof, Theorem 3.9 and the introduction.
issues.overall_effect: Estimate (3.6) is unsupported as written. The proof establishes it with the best-approximation term measured on K.
issues.title: Stated infimum over L^2(K_0) is not what the proof gives (it gives L^2(K))
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol change in the statement matches what is proved. All later uses already employ the L^2(K) form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with their axes scaled by a factor of $1.4$

issues.failure_explanation: The fifth ellipse of K_0 has axes (0.025, 0.0725). Scaling by 1.4 gives (0.035, 0.1015), but the text lists (0.035, 0.0875) for K, which corresponds to 0.0625 and not 0.0725. The other five ellipses are consistent with the factor 1.4. The experimental setup for Example 3 is therefore internally contradictory, and the geometry actually used for K_0 and K is ambiguous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the correct axis for either K_0 or K so that the 1.4 scaling holds (0.0625 versus 0.0725 for K_0, or 0.1015 for K), and confirm which geometry was used in the computations.
issues.overall_effect: Example 3 cannot be reproduced unambiguously. The reported errors depend on the sizes of K_0 and K, so their meaning is uncertain. No theorem is affected.
issues.title: Porous-defect geometry inconsistent with the stated 1.4 scaling
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local data correction in the description of one numerical example. It touches no theoretical claim.
